page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is a specialized high-performance computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System architecture. It features 48 dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 physical cores operating at a base clock frequency of 3.7 GHz with a single execution thread per core. The host provides 768 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a resource ratio of 16 GB RAM per dedicated physical core. Network capabilities include a 150 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while the instance contains no local NVMe storage drives and no discrete hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark analyses show top-tier multi-core processor execution and memory subsystem throughput. In stress-ng multi-core testing, the instance achieved a score of 147,294.74, placing it in the top 10% of benchmarked systems. Large-block memory bandwidth tests recorded uncached reads of 695.05 GB/sec and uncached writes of 347.3 GB/sec. Highly parallel operations such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 636.8 GB/sec and software compilation using Clang also reached top 10% performance categories. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 extensions with VNNI and BF16 support, alongside VAES instruction sets for cryptographic processing.

The hardware configuration provides high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bandwidth-bound parallel applications by eliminating the expense of bundled local disks or unneeded GPU resources while maintaining high memory density. The primary tradeoff is the requirement for network-attached storage solution architectures for disk persistence. While single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and static web serving demonstrate average performance, the instance delivers maximum efficiency for parallel computational fluid dynamics, physics models, Clang software builds, and high-concurrency Redis caching.
description: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is a dedicated high-performance computing server instance built on the AWS Nitro system. Powered by 48 AMD EPYC 9R14 physical cores operating at 3.7 GHz with single-threaded execution, it features 768 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz and 150 Gbps baseline network throughput. The instance incorporates AVX-512 vector instruction extensions but omits local storage and discrete GPUs. Benchmark results place hpc7a.24xlarge in the top 10% for multi-core compute in stress-ng, large-block memory read/write bandwidth, and multi-threaded decompression, alongside top-tier Redis SET operation rates. While single-threaded tasks show average metrics and disk I/O relies on network-attached storage, its high memory ratio of 16 GB per physical core and high interconnect throughput offer qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound, parallel execution. It is well suited for computational physics, distributed engineering simulations, large Clang compilation tasks, and high-throughput key-value data stores.
